answer: In an attestation graph with capped per-edge influence, trust propagates through bounded random walks from trusted seeds, not by counting identities. If a sybil set S has a sparse external cut, its conductance, Φ(S)=cut(S,V\\S)/vol(S), is low; min-cut and walk-crossing bounds then limit trusted paths entering S and hence its aggregate voting weight. Mirror, dune, and comet may label nodes, but labels alone confer no trust.
